used.text: Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 • StartFindService ([SWS_CM_00123], [SWS_CM_00623]) • SetServiceStateChangeHandler ([SWS_CM_01074], [SWS_CM_01076]) ⌋ 7.5.8 Registering get handlers for fields For the registering get handlers for fields C++ API reference, see chapter 8.4.3.2.3.2 and 8.4.3.2.3.1. [SWS_CM_10412] Invoking GetHandlers Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00218 ⌈ The registered GetHandler shall be called by the implementation whenever the Communication Management receives a Get() . ⌋ [SWS_CM_00824] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for GetHandlers calls by the client ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each Get() of the respective field class shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (cf. ServiceInterfaceDe- ploymentElement.minimumSendInterval), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive calls of GetHandlers by the client, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given Get() call for a Field in the network. If the application tries to Field::Get() a field value, by in- voking Get() of the respective field class, ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the Get() call the underlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the Get() handler has never been invoked before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the Field::Get() call by handing it over to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com shall discard the Field::Get() call, and return the error code ComErrc::kMinimumSendIn- tervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via the ara:: core::Future of the Get() of the respective field class. The Minimum Send Inter- val shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually invokes the Field::Get() call and not by the server/provider, which returns the corresponding Field value by answering the Field::Get() call. If the configured Minimum Send In- terval (ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.minimumSendInterval) of a Field::Get () of the respective field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding Field::Get() . ⌋ [SWS_CM_00825] Default value of Minimum Send Interval and disabling Mini- mum Send Interval monitoring for GetHandlers for Clients ⌈ If the configured Mini- mum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendIn- terval ) of a Get() of the respective field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding Field::Get() , 286 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement
